historical_reviews.port1_context: Row 1906 is BF3 Port 1. Even if both ports use identical wording, its cable, peer, lanes and LED wiring are separate and provide no Port 2 acceptance evidence.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-36 requires exact physical topology and measurable behavior; ED-38 prohibits undocumented commands, traffic, resets and cable actions and reserves verdicts.

original_test_intent: Verify BF3 Port 2 physical LED color and cadence for connected, disconnected, I/O-active and owner-commanded states.
original_method: A qualified on-site operator labels Port 2 and its peer, isolates stimuli to that path, executes only approved cable/I/O/command transitions, captures synchronized visual and link evidence, and restores the original link.
manual_activity: An on-site operator proves the labeled Port 2 path, performs the approved cable, Port-2-scoped I/O and amber-command cases, captures synchronized video, and confirms link and service restoration.
required_inputs: Exact BF3 device serial/PCI identity, Port 2 cage/lane mapping and peer endpoint
Cable/transceiver identity, ownership, redundancy and approved handling power state
Proof that test traffic is isolated to Port 2 rather than Port 1 or another path
Green/amber emitter or bicolor semantics and expected connected/disconnected combinations
Bounded Port-2 I/O stimulus plus expected green cadence, duty and observation time
Reviewed Port-2-targeted Amber Blink command, effects, duration and cleanup
Passive link state/speed/width/error counters and service health sources
Camera/color/timing standard plus independent fabric/network recovery
safety_requirements: Trace and label both ends of Port 2 before any disconnect; do not rely on chassis ordering alone
Verify redundancy and service impact and never remove an active sole path
Ensure traffic and any LED command target Port 2 specifically; never borrow Port 1 control syntax without approval
Do not infer visual color from link state or command success
Stop on wrong-port response, failed renegotiation, link errors, thermal/power anomaly or unsafe access
Restore original cable/transceiver placement and verify Port 2 service independently
agent_execution_scope: Verify exact Port 2 cage/lane/peer identity and isolation from Port 1
Collect passive before/after link identity, negotiation, counters and service evidence
Organize synchronized operator video for each approved visual state
Check that I/O and command evidence names Port 2 and that restoration is complete
Perform no cable handling, traffic generation, LED command, reset, power action, retry or verdict
engineer_actions: Approve Port 2 topology, cable/transceiver and safe impact plan
Define emitter semantics and connected/disconnected color combinations
Approve Port-2-scoped traffic and exact amber-blink command
Review visual/link/restoration evidence and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Correctly non-runnable for direct acceptance because color/cadence and cable routing require human observation; no safe Port-2 stimulus command is supplied.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use a labeled manual Port 2 matrix with synchronized video and passive link evidence; keep any traffic or amber command separately approved and operator-controlled.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BF3 Port 2, connected/disconnected plus green/amber solid/blink states and 15/5-minute estimates remain.

modernized_recommendation.status: MANUAL PORT2 LED REVIEW REQUIRES LANE/PEER PROOF AND PORT-SCOPED STIMULI
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Trace Port 2 end to end, capture its lane/peer and cable labels, then record LED and link telemetry together while applying only Port-2-scoped approved transitions.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds lane-level path proof and stimulus isolation so neighboring Port 1 activity cannot create false evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Port 1 observations remain separate even on the same BF3 device; OSFP Channel 1 in the next row is another unrelated physical indicator.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Multipath routing can send generated I/O over Port 1 while Port 2 remains idle. Without per-port counters or peer confirmation, a blinking Port 2 LED may reflect management or training activity rather than the intended data stimulus.

project_override_considerations: If port LEDs are shared across cages or lanes, the owner must define the aggregation rule and a stimulus proving Port 2 contribution. Otherwise individual-port acceptance is not supportable.
expected_evidence: Approved BF3/Port 2 cage/lane/cable/transceiver/peer map and redundancy plan
Emitter semantics plus connected/disconnected, Port-2 I/O and amber-command matrix
Timestamped contextual and close video tied to Port 2 labels and stimulus timeline
Per-port or peer-confirmed link negotiation, counters, events and restored service

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Green and Amber Solid share cable-state wording but may be separate emitters or a defined combined state; exact LED topology and criteria are missing, not conclusively contradictory.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The Port 2 visual purpose is identifiable and manually executable once the owner supplies end-to-end topology, isolated stimuli and recovery.

review_improvement: Adds end-to-end Port 2 lane/peer proof and stimulus isolation to prevent neighboring-port activity from being accepted as target evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: On a multipath system, application I/O can be rerouted away from Port 2 while the operator believes that port is under test. Port-specific counters or peer evidence must therefore accompany the visual record; otherwise either a false lack of blinking or unrelated training activity can be misclassified.
